content.what_it_is: MATLAB function that parses map-rendering options (L169-L215), derives a Web-Mercator-compatible center and zoom from WGS84 axes (L232-L358), builds and downloads a Google Static Maps request (L360-L436), converts indexed imagery to RGB and optionally resizes it (L447-L460), projects pixels through EPSG:900913 and nearest-neighbour resamples them onto a latitude/longitude grid (L462-L485), then either plots the map beneath existing graphics with refresh callbacks (L487-L533) or returns longitude, latitude, and image arrays (L534-L537). Subfunctions implement Mercator conversions (L543-L555), grid interpolation (L558-L602), zoom/pan refresh (L605-L618), and figure-resize refresh (L621-L640).

unresolved: L459 already applies resize to imag; L463-L464 then measure that resized image, but L477-L478 multiply those measured dimensions by resize again before L485 resamples to the uniform grid. For resize values other than 1, the returned/plotted grid therefore applies the requested dimension factor twice (for example resize=2 produces another twofold output dimension after imresize).

L229 stores only the caller's original varargin. The zoom/pan callback obtains the event axes at L609 but discards that handle when it reloads params at L616 and recursively calls plot_google_map(params{:}) at L617; when the original call omitted Axis, the recursive call falls back to gca at L152 and can refresh a different axes in a multi-axes figure. The figure-resize callback separately adds the missing Axis at L635-L636, exposing the inconsistent callback interface.

Only scale is range-checked at L179-L182. resize and alphaData are accepted directly at L184 and L188; resize is later passed to imresize at L459 and used as a divisor at L468, so zero or negative values reach an invalid resize/division path instead of being rejected at the option boundary.

Degenerate axes spans pass the plausibility test at L233, yield zero projected extents at L269-L270, and can cause division by zero in the aspect corrections at L286 or L302 and zero minRes in the zoom calculation at L341-L346; there is no nonzero-span guard before those formulas.
